# Results — Study 670 (Bollinger-Squeeze)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**"TTM Squeeze"**: when the Bollinger Bands contract to sit INSIDE the Keltner Channel, a big
directional move is coming, so trade the breakout when the bands re-expand. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of
**2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprints `a86d937ba301` (SPY) /
`bffd139860b4` (QQQ) / `c6d8143586a8` (IWM) / `e2f0408ffa53` (DIA) / `9d2b65b169e8` (GLD) —
basket fingerprint `96534419f523`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted OHLC, **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (5,406 rows each), 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Bands | Bollinger: SMA(20) ± 2.0·std(20) of close. Keltner: EMA(20) ± 1.5·ATR(20) (Wilder-style, rolling mean of True Range) |
| Squeeze | ON when `bb_upper < kc_upper` and `bb_lower > kc_lower`; **release** = the first non-squeeze bar after ≥ 5 consecutive squeeze bars |
| Direction | sign of a causal OLS slope of close over the trailing 20 bars, evaluated on the release bar (no look-ahead) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* (signal vs matched random-timing / same-direction-mix control); one-sample HAC (Newey-West) *t* vs 0; one-sample *t* of the forward/trailing vol ratio vs 1 |
| Execution / costs | signal on the release bar's close, position entered at the **next bar's open** (one documented lag); one-way cost × NAV × 2 legs per round trip (5 / 10 bps); short legs pay a 20 bps/yr borrow accrual, prorated by holding period |
| Events | **111** squeeze-release events pooled across the 5-ticker basket (SPY 20, QQQ 18, IWM 31, DIA 25, GLD 17); squeeze bars are 3.7–7.9% of each tape |
| Data quirks (named) | no survivorship — SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA/GLD are long-lived, still-listed ETFs, not a current-membership panel; adjusted (total-return) OHLC, so no split/dividend artefacts fake a band pierce |

## Test 1 — does volatility genuinely EXPAND after the release?

Two distinct comparisons, kept separate on purpose: (a) forward-10-day realized vol vs the
vol *during the squeeze itself* (near-tautological — a squeeze IS low trailing vol by
construction, so "reversion to average" is close to definitional) and (b) forward-10-day
realized vol vs a **matched random-day control** on the same tape — the honest test of whether
the release specifically *times* the expansion better than any other day.

| ticker | fwd-10d vol | during-squeeze vol | ratio | one-sample *t* (ratio vs 1) | random-day fwd vol | Welch *t* (release vs random) | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 1.067%/day | 0.813%/day | 1.32× | +2.13 | 0.959%/day | +0.59 | 20 |
| QQQ | 1.091%/day | 0.974%/day | 1.13× | +1.49 | 1.169%/day | −0.70 | 18 |
| IWM | 1.326%/day | 1.271%/day | 1.02× | +0.26 | 1.304%/day | +0.11 | 31 |
| DIA | 0.969%/day | 0.811%/day | 1.19× | +1.64 | 0.902%/day | +0.43 | 25 |
| GLD | 0.781%/day | 0.929%/day | 0.84× | **−2.30** | 1.006%/day | **−2.14** | 17 |
| **POOLED** | **1.077%/day** | | | | **1.068%/day** | **+0.12** | **111** |

The tautological ratio (a) is mildly positive for 4 of 5 tickers but only individually
significant for SPY (*t* = +2.13) and actually **inverts** for GLD (0.84×, *t* = −2.30) — vol
was *lower* after the release than during the squeeze itself. More importantly: the honest
comparison (b), pooled across the whole basket, shows **no incremental timing information at
all** — Welch *t* = **+0.12**. A squeeze release does not predict more forward volatility than
picking any other day on the same tape and looking 10 days out. Markets are volatility-
clustered everywhere on this tape, not just after a documented squeeze; a random day's forward
window reverts toward average vol just as readily as a squeeze-release day's does.

## Test 2 — the directional breakout trade

Enter next bar's open in the sign of the release-bar slope, hold 10 days, one-way costs × 2
legs, short legs pay borrow. Pinned against a **matched random-timing, same-direction-mix
control** (same tickers, same event count, the identical multiset of long/short calls reshuffled
onto random dates) — isolating whether squeeze *timing* adds anything beyond the instrument's
generic drift and the direction mix's own bias.

| cost | signal (net/trade) | HAC *t* vs 0 | win rate | random-mix control | Welch *t* (signal − control) | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | **−36.5 bps** | −1.00 | 44.1% | −44.4 bps | **+0.15** | 111 |
| 10 bps | −46.5 bps | −1.27 | 43.2% | −54.4 bps | +0.15 | 111 |

The signal loses money net of costs — but so does the random-timing control with the *same*
direction mix, and the **gap between them is statistically nothing** (Welch *t* = +0.15). The
squeeze's timing adds zero information over picking the same long/short calls on random dates;
whatever drag the ledger shows is generic (see the per-ticker breakdown), not squeeze-specific.

## Test 3 — per-ticker breakdown (hold 10d, 5 bps)

| ticker | n | mean net | win rate | HAC *t* vs 0 | Welch *t* vs random |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 20 | −17.2 bps | 55.0% | −0.25 | −0.70 |
| QQQ | 18 | −56.8 bps | 55.6% | −0.81 | +1.36 |
| IWM | 31 | +78.0 bps | 54.8% | +0.82 | +0.78 |
| DIA | 25 | −105.8 bps | 28.0% | **−3.27** | −1.30 |
| GLD | 17 | −144.7 bps | 23.5% | −1.75 | −0.25 |

DIA's raw HAC *t* (−3.27) looks alarming in isolation — but vs its own matched random control
it is **not** significant (*t* = −1.30): DIA simply had a rough run of dates around its squeeze
releases, the same drag any random 25-trade sample from that window would have picked up. No
ticker clears the bar vs its own random control in either direction.

## Test 4 — parameter robustness sweep

Pooled directional Welch *t* (signal vs matched random control) across BB std ∈ {1.5, 2.0, 2.5}
× KC multiplier ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} × hold days ∈ {5, 10, 20} = 27 combinations, 5 bps costs.

| | value |
|---|--:|
| combos tested | 27 |
| combos with \|Welch *t*\| ≥ 2 | **0 / 27 (0%)** |
| Welch *t* range | [−1.60, +0.67] |
| mean Welch *t* | −0.40 |
| best-\|*t*\| combo | BB=2.5, KC=1.5, hold=20d → *t* = −1.60 (n=23) |

Not one of the 27 reasonable parameterisations clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar — including the
single best-looking one, which is negative (the breakout direction would have LOST against its
own random-mix control). This is the signature of noise, not a fragile-but-real effect: nothing
in the neighbourhood of the "standard" TTM parameters comes close.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A deterministic regime-switching tape: **quiet** (mean ~70 bars) is genuinely mean-reverting
around a live-reset anchor — a real range-bound consolidation that produces a true BB-inside-KC
squeeze, not a coincidence of noise; **loud** (mean ~15 bars) turns reversion off and raises vol
— the bands re-expand and a release fires a few bars in. A TUNABLE knob `continuation` plants a
directional drift that persists for 15 loud sessions after the regime flips.

| world | Welch *t* (signal vs matched random control) |
|---|--:|
| null (continuation = 0), **10 seeds** | mean **−0.43** (sd 0.87), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/10 seeds** |
| planted continuation = 1.0 (seed 670) | **+6.96** (n = 32 events) |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up hard on a planted directional-continuation
effect (+1,208 bps/trade vs −136 bps on the control). *(A faithful-engine / power check only —
never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The breakout direction does not call the next move: Welch *t* = **+0.15**
  vs a matched random-timing, same-direction-mix control at 5 and 10 bps costs, and **0 of 27**
  reasonable band/hold parameterisations clear \|*t*\| ≥ 2. No ticker's directional edge is
  distinguishable from its own random control.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net returns are negative (−36.5 to −46.5 bps/trade) at realistic
  costs, and indistinguishable from a random-timing control with the identical direction mix —
  there is no edge here to scale, only costs to pay for noise.
- **Does the squeeze even call MORE volatility than a random day? — BUSTED.** Pooled forward-vol
  Welch *t* vs a matched random day is **+0.12** — no incremental timing information. The
  "vol WILL expand" framing is true only in the trivial, near-tautological sense of reverting
  away from the squeeze's own contracted baseline (positive but individually significant only
  for SPY, and it actually *inverts* for GLD) — not in the sense that matters for a trader: a
  squeeze release does not predict more expansion than any other day on the tape.
